sections.h2: What kind of county is St. Lucie County for a seller?
sections.html:
St. Lucie County grew from 329,226 people in April 2020 to an estimated 402,449 in July 2025, a 22.2 percent gain. The Census Bureau lists 571.66 square miles of land and 575.9 residents per square mile in 2020.

The 2020 to 2024 median value of owner-occupied homes was $347,300 and median gross rent was $1,585. About 78.6 percent of homes are owner-occupied and 24.9 percent of residents are 65 or older, which makes the senior and deferral options below worth a close read.

sections.h2: Who handles property tax in St. Lucie County?
sections.html:
Three county offices matter. The Saint Lucie County Property Appraiser values property and processes exemptions; the St. Lucie County Tax Collector sends bills and takes payments; and the Clerk of the Circuit Court runs the Value Adjustment Board process and records deeds.

The property appraiser's office lists a phone line of 772-462-1000 on its TRIM notice page for questions about value or exemptions. Exemption questions belong with the appraiser, not the collector.

sections.h2: When does the St. Lucie County TRIM notice arrive, and what can an owner do with it?
sections.html:
The property appraiser mails the notice in mid-August to the owner of record of every parcel. It is an estimate rather than a bill, built from proposed millage rates, the January 1 value and any exemptions.

The notice shows three columns: last year's figures, what taxes would be if each taxing authority kept its revenue flat, and what they would be at the proposed rate. It also lists budget hearing dates and the deadline for a Value Adjustment Board petition over value, classification or an exemption. For 2026 that deadline was September 8, which has passed. Future deadlines are printed on each year's notice.

A buyer should note that the notice explains why a bill jumps after a purchase: reassessment on January 1 and removal of the prior owner's exemptions and caps.

sections.h2: What are the St. Lucie County tax discounts and deadlines?
sections.html:
The tax collector publishes a month-by-month list. The early-payment discount shrinks from 4 percent in November to 3 percent in December, 2 percent in January and 1 percent in February, which the state revenue department prints the same way.

The collector's calendar also gives January 31 as its deadline for homestead tax deferral, while the state's general guidance names March 31 following the assessment year, so ask the St. Lucie office which date governs your application. March 1 is the deadline to file new homestead exemptions with the property appraiser.

  • November: 4 percent discount, bills issued.
  • December: 3 percent.
  • January: 2 percent.
  • February: 1 percent.
  • April 1: unpaid taxes turn delinquent.

sections.h2: How does Save Our Homes affect a St. Lucie County sale?
sections.html:
The appraiser's TRIM guide explains it plainly: a property bought in a given year is reassessed and the prior owner's exemptions and caps are removed, which can lift the tax bill. For sellers, that is the reason a listing's current tax figure understates what a buyer will pay.

The Save Our Homes cap limits assessment growth on a homestead to 3 percent or the CPI change, whichever is lower, and starts accruing after the first year of homestead. The 2026 cap on the state's chart was 2.7 percent. Sellers who buy another Florida home can transfer up to $500,000 of the accumulated difference through portability, using Form DR-501T by March 1, provided the new homestead is set up within three years.

sections.h2: What closing charges come with a St. Lucie County deed?
sections.html:
Documentary stamp tax is 70 cents per $100 of consideration, according to Florida Statutes 201.02 and the revenue department. The clerk collects it when the deed is recorded.

Every party to the deed is liable, so the purchase contract should assign it. Recording fees are $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each additional page, plus other per-page charges listed in the fee statute. A deed in lieu of foreclosure or a trustee's deed is taxable too, while a personal representative's deed under a probated will is not.

sections.h2: Which tax breaks can a St. Lucie County homeowner claim?
sections.html:
The standard homestead exemption is up to $50,000 under state law, split into a first $25,000 that covers school taxes and an added slice for non-school taxes on assessed value above $50,000. The added slice is indexed to inflation each January 1.

Beyond that, the state lists several options an owner may qualify for:

  • An added exemption for owners 65 or older where a local ordinance allows it and household income is within the limit.
  • A $5,000 reduction for disabled former servicemembers rated 10 percent or more.
  • A homestead discount equal to the VA disability percentage for veterans 65 or older with a permanent service-connected disability.
  • Homestead tax deferral, with the tax collector, for taxes above a share of household income.

Ask the property appraiser which of these apply to your parcel before the March 1 deadline.

sections.h2: What should an heir or seller who lived elsewhere check in St. Lucie County?
sections.html:
Start with whether homestead is still in place. State rules say homestead ends if the house is rented, stops being the permanent home or the owner leaves Florida as a permanent resident. Renting the home is the usual way owners lose it without noticing.

Then look at the title. A personal representative's deed under a probated will is listed as not taxable for documentary stamps, but a deed with no probate has no estate planning exception. Confirm the parcel number on the property appraiser's record card, which the appraiser's site offers through its real estate search. Finally ask the tax collector for a payoff, since taxes unpaid after April 1 can reach the certificate stage and a certificate holder may later apply for a tax deed.

These steps cost little and keep a sale of a St. Lucie County house from stalling at the closing table.

sections.h2: What if a St. Lucie County owner is behind on taxes?
sections.html:
Taxes become delinquent April 1, and certificates are sold by June 1. The lowest interest bid wins the certificate, and unsold ones go to the county at the maximum rate.

Certificate holders can request a tax deed two years after April 1 of the year of issue. A homestead's opening bid includes half the latest assessed value. Contact the tax collector for a current payoff, because a sale cannot close cleanly while a certificate is outstanding.

  • Request a tax certificate search from the title company.
  • Ask whether a homestead deferral lien exists.
  • Pay delinquent amounts from the sale proceeds at closing.

faqs.q: When is the St. Lucie County homestead filing deadline?
faqs.a: March 1 of the tax year, filed with the property appraiser. You must have owned and lived in the home as your permanent residence on January 1.

faqs.q: Does St. Lucie County mail the tax bill in November?
faqs.a: Yes, bills go out in November from the tax collector, when the 4 percent early-payment discount applies.

faqs.q: Why did my St. Lucie County taxes jump after buying?
faqs.a: The property is reassessed to market value and the prior owner's exemptions and caps are removed, which the property appraiser's TRIM guide describes.

faqs.q: Who do I call in St. Lucie County about my property value?
faqs.a: The Property Appraiser's office, which lists 772-462-1000 on its TRIM notice page.

faqs.q: Does St. Lucie County have a deed transfer tax?
faqs.a: Yes, Florida's documentary stamp tax at 70 cents per $100 of consideration, paid to the clerk at recording.
